import pytest


def stamp(ts: int) -> str:
    """Format a Unix timestamp (seconds since the epoch) as UTC `HH:MM:SS`.

    Uses a 24-hour clock with zero-padded fields. Only the time of day is
    shown, so the value wraps every 86400 seconds. Negative timestamps wrap
    backwards, so -1 gives "23:59:59". The function is pure and does no I/O.
    """
    secs = ts % 86400
    hours, rem = divmod(secs, 3600)
    minutes, seconds = divmod(rem, 60)
    return f"{hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{seconds:02d}"


def test_epoch() -> None:
    assert stamp(0) == "00:00:00"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ts", "expected"),
    [
        (1, "00:00:01"),
        (59, "00:00:59"),
        (60, "00:01:00"),
        (3599, "00:59:59"),
        (3600, "01:00:00"),
        (36610, "10:10:10"),
        (86399, "23:59:59"),
    ],
)
def test_within_first_day(ts: int, expected: str) -> None:
    assert stamp(ts) == expected


def test_zero_padding() -> None:
    assert stamp(3661) == "01:01:01"


def test_known_timestamp() -> None:
    # 2023-11-14 22:13:20 UTC
    assert stamp(1_700_000_000) == "22:13:20"


def test_wraps_at_day_boundary() -> None:
    assert stamp(86400) == "00:00:00"
    assert stamp(86401) == "00:00:01"
    assert stamp(86400 * 365 + 3661) == "01:01:01"


def test_negative_wraps_backwards() -> None:
    assert stamp(-1) == "23:59:59"
    assert stamp(-86400) == "00:00:00"
    assert stamp(-3600) == "23:00:00"


def test_returns_str_of_fixed_width() -> None:
    for ts in (0, 5, 12345, 99_999_999_999, -7):
        out = stamp(ts)
        assert isinstance(out, str)
        assert len(out) == 8
        assert out[2] == ":" and out[5] == ":"
